description: The date on which the operational risk event was first identified or discovered by the bank, which may differ significantly from the event date for latent losses. Used to measure detection lag and assess control effectiveness.

description: The date on which the operational risk loss event actually occurred or commenced. This is the principal real-world event date used for SMA capital charge period allocation and regulatory reporting. Distinct from discovery date and accounting date.

description: Detailed narrative description of the operational risk event, including what happened, how it was identified, and the immediate impact. Supports root cause analysis, regulatory examination responses, and internal audit reviews.

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the operational risk event by the GRC platform or internal loss database (e.g., ORE-2024-00123). Used for cross-system reconciliation and regulatory reporting submissions to OCC/Fed/PRA.

description: Current lifecycle status of the operational risk event record. 'open' indicates active loss event under investigation; 'under_review' indicates root cause analysis in progress; 'closed' indicates fully resolved and signed off; 'near_miss' indicates no financial loss but control failure identified; 'pending_recovery' indicates awaiting insurance or third-party recovery.

description: Short, descriptive title summarizing the nature of the operational risk event (e.g., 'Unauthorized Wire Transfer — Treasury Operations', 'System Outage — Payment Processing Hub'). Used for management reporting and GRC dashboard display.

description: Reference identifier linking this internal loss event to a corresponding record in an external operational risk loss data consortium (e.g., ORX — Operational Riskdata eXchange Association). Supports benchmarking of internal loss experience against industry peers.

description: Total gross financial loss incurred from the operational risk event before any recoveries, expressed in the reporting currency. description: Status of any legal proceedings or litigation associated with the operational risk event. reference: FASB ASC 450 Contingencies; IFRS IAS 37 Provisions; OCC Supervisory Guidance; SOX

description: Financial provision or reserve established in the general ledger for potential legal liability arising from the operational risk event. Recognized per IFRS IAS 37 or FASB ASC 450 when outflow is probable and estimable.

description: Date on which the recovery amount was received or recognized, whether from insurance, legal settlement, or third-party reimbursement. Used for cash flow timing analysis and SMA recovery component allocation.

description: Flag indicating whether the gross loss amount meets or exceeds the minimum loss data threshold (typically USD 20,000 per BCBS guidance) required for inclusion in the SMA Loss Component calculation and external loss data consortium submissions.

description: Flag indicating whether this record represents a near-miss incident (potential loss that was averted) rather than an actual realized loss event. Near-miss events have zero gross loss but are captured for control environment assessment and KRI monitoring.

description: Net financial loss after deducting all recoveries from the gross loss amount (gross_loss_amount minus recovery_amount). This is the final economic impact figure used for P&L attribution, RAROC calculation, and management reporting.

description: Total amount recovered from all sources (insurance, legal settlements, third-party reimbursements, collateral liquidation) following the operational risk loss event. Subtracted from gross loss to derive net loss.

CET1 ratio threshold at which Additional Tier 1 capital instruments would be written down or converted, expressed as a percentage.

description: Starting Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio at the beginning of the planning horizon, expressed as a percentage.

description: Narrative description of planned capital actions including issuances, redemptions, dividends, and buybacks over the planning horizon.
Free-text comments or notes regarding the capital plan, including rationale for key assumptions or regulatory feedback.
Timestamp when the capital plan record was first created in the system.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in the capital plan (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

description: Projected net income over the planning horizon under the specified scenario, in millions of base currency.

Version identifier for the capital plan to track revisions and resubmissions (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.1 Revised').
Total planned capital issuance (common equity, preferred stock, subordinated debt) over the planning horizon, in millions of base currency.
Total planned capital redemptions (preferred stock, subordinated debt) over the planning horizon, in millions of base currency.
Total planned common stock dividend distributions over the planning horizon, in millions of base currency.
Planned dividend payout ratio as a percentage of net income over the planning horizon.
Total planned share repurchase amount over the planning horizon, in millions of base currency.
End date of the multi-year capital planning horizon covered by this plan.
Start date of the multi-year capital planning horizon covered by this plan.
Projected pre-provision net revenue over the planning horizon under the specified scenario, in millions of base currency.

business_glossary_term: Projected Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) Growth Rate Year 2

Date the capital plan was submitted to the Federal Reserve for CCAR/DFAST review.

description: Foreign key linking to hr.employee. Business justification: Capital ratio calculations require CFO/CRO approval for Basel III regulatory submissions and capital adequacy reporting. approved_by_user text field should be FK to employee_id for regulatory audit tr

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_regulatory_filing. Business justification: Capital ratios are reported in Call Reports (FFIEC 031/041), FR Y-9C, and Basel III reports. Direct linkage enables audit trail from calculated ratio to submitted filing, essential for regulatory comp

Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: Capital ratios calculated per regulatory jurisdiction for Basel compliance. Link enables jurisdiction-specific capital buffers (CCyB, G-SIB), CCAR/DFAST applicability, and regulatory submission routin
Reference to the legal entity for which capital ratios are calculated. Links to the legal entity master.

Foreign key linking to reference.regulatory_taxonomy. Business justification: Capital ratio reporting follows regulatory taxonomy (Basel III/IV, FFIEC 031). Link enables taxonomy version lookup, XBRL tagging, data point mapping, and regulatory submission validation.

Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Capital ratios reported in regulatory currency (USD for US banks, EUR for EU banks). Link enables multi-entity consolidation, FX revaluation for group reporting, and regulatory submission validation.

business_glossary_term: Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO) Target Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio
description: The internal ALCO-approved target CET1 ratio, typically set above regulatory minimums to provide a management buffer for business volatility and growth.
The approval status of the capital ratio calculation and capital plan within the internal governance process.
The date and time when this capital ratio record was approved by the authorized approver.
Indicates whether the CET1 ratio has breached the contractual trigger level for AT1 instrument write-down or conversion (typically 5.125% or 7.0% depending on instrument terms).
reference: Basel III Framework - AT1 Instrument Requirements

description: The methodology used to calculate credit risk RWA: Standardized Approach (SA), Internal Ratings-Based Foundation (IRB-F), or Internal Ratings-Based Advanced (IRB-A).
reference: Basel III Framework - Credit Risk Approaches

description: The capital conservation buffer requirement, expressed as a percentage of RWA. Standard requirement is 2.5% of RWA in CET1 capital above the minimum.
reference: Basel III Framework - Capital Conservation Buffer

description: The amount of new capital issuance (common equity, AT1, or Tier 2 instruments) planned or executed during the reporting period.
The amount of capital instrument redemptions (AT1 or Tier 2 instruments) planned or executed during the reporting period.
The absolute amount of CET1 capital held above the minimum regulatory requirement plus buffers, representing the management buffer or excess capital.
The total Common Equity Tier 1 capital amount, representing the highest quality capital consisting of common shares, retained earnings, and other comprehensive income, net of regulatory adjustments.
The CET1 capital ratio, calculated as CET1 capital divided by total RWA, expressed as a percentage. Regulatory minimum is 4.5% under Basel III.
reference: Basel III Framework - CET1 Ratio Requirement

description: Free-text comments or notes regarding the capital ratio calculation, assumptions, or capital actions for this reporting period.
Indicates whether the capital ratio is calculated at consolidated group level, solo legal entity level, or sub-consolidated level.
The countercyclical capital buffer requirement, expressed as a percentage of RWA. Ranges from 0% to 2.5% and varies by jurisdiction based on credit cycle conditions.
The date and time when this capital ratio record was first created in the system.
Risk-weighted assets arising from credit risk exposures, calculated using either the Standardized Approach (SA) or Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approach.
reference: Basel III Framework - Credit Risk RWA

description: The additional capital surcharge for Global Systemically Important Banks, ranging from 1.0% to 3.5% of RWA based on systemic importance score.
The date and time when this capital ratio record was last modified or updated.
The leverage ratio, calculated as Tier 1 capital divided by total exposure measure (on- and off-balance sheet exposures), expressed as a percentage. Regulatory minimum is 3.0% under Basel III.
reference: Basel III Framework - Leverage Ratio Requirement

description: Risk-weighted assets arising from market risk exposures in the trading book, calculated under the Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) or legacy market risk framework.
reference: Basel III Framework - Market Risk RWA / FRTB

description: Risk-weighted assets arising from operational risk, calculated using the Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) or legacy approaches.
reference: Basel III Framework - Operational Risk RWA / SMA

description: The planned share repurchase amount for the reporting period under the capital plan.
The planned common stock dividend distribution amount for the reporting period under the capital plan.

business_glossary_term: Projected Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio Year 1
description: The projected CET1 ratio for the first year of the capital planning horizon under the specified scenario.
reference: CCAR and DFAST Capital Planning Requirements

business_glossary_term: Projected Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio Year 2
description: The projected CET1 ratio for the second year of the capital planning horizon under the specified scenario.
reference: CCAR and DFAST Capital Planning Requirements

business_glossary_term: Projected Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio Year 3
description: The projected CET1 ratio for the third year of the capital planning horizon under the specified scenario.
reference: CCAR and DFAST Capital Planning Requirements

description: The assumed annual growth rate for RWA in the capital planning scenario, expressed as a percentage.
reference: CCAR and DFAST Capital Planning Requirements

business_glossary_term: Regulatory Minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio
description: The applicable regulatory minimum CET1 ratio including all buffers, representing the threshold below which capital distribution restrictions apply.
reference: Basel III Framework / Federal Reserve Requirements

description: Indicates whether this capital ratio record was submitted to regulatory authorities as part of formal reporting (CCAR, DFAST, Basel III Pillar 3).
The date for which the capital ratio is calculated and reported. Typically month-end or quarter-end for regulatory submissions.
The reporting period identifier in format YYYY-QN for quarterly or YYYY-MNN for monthly reporting cycles.
The stress scenario or planning scenario under which the capital ratio is calculated. Actual represents current position, base/adverse/severely_adverse represent CCAR/DFAST stress scenarios.
reference: CCAR and DFAST Stress Testing Requirements

description: The name of the source system from which the capital ratio data was extracted, typically the Risk Management Platform or Regulatory Reporting Platform.
The date on which this capital ratio was submitted to regulatory authorities.
The total Tier 1 capital amount, comprising CET1 capital plus Additional Tier 1 (AT1) instruments such as perpetual non-cumulative preferred stock.
The Tier 1 capital ratio, calculated as Tier 1 capital divided by total RWA, expressed as a percentage. Regulatory minimum is 6.0% under Basel III.
reference: Basel III Framework - Tier 1 Ratio Requirement

description: The total Tier 2 capital amount, comprising subordinated debt, hybrid instruments, and loan loss reserves up to regulatory limits.
The sum of all capital buffer requirements (conservation, countercyclical, G-SIB surcharge), expressed as a percentage of RWA.
reference: Basel III Framework - Combined Buffer Requirement

description: The sum of Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital, representing the total regulatory capital available to absorb losses.
reference: Basel III Framework - Total Capital Definition

description: The total capital ratio, calculated as total capital divided by total RWA, expressed as a percentage. Regulatory minimum is 8.0% under Basel III.
reference: Basel III Framework - Total Capital Ratio Requirement

description: The total exposure measure used in the leverage ratio calculation, comprising on-balance sheet exposures, derivative exposures, securities financing transaction exposures, and off-balance sheet items.
reference: Basel III Framework - Leverage Ratio Exposure Measure

description: The sum of credit, market, and operational risk-weighted assets, representing the total risk exposure for capital adequacy calculation.
Unique identifier for the debt issuance record. Primary key for the debt issuance product.

Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Debt issuances denominated in specific currencies for funding and NSFR. Link enables currency validation, FX hedging, NSFR ASF calculation by currency, and multi-currency funding cost reporting.

Foreign key linking to treasury.funding_plan. Business justification: Debt issuance is the execution of a funding plan. The funding_plan product captures the strategic funding plan (target_issuance_amount, target_maturity_profile, target_cost_of_funds_rate), while debt_

Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: Debt issuances are liabilities requiring GL account mapping for financial reporting, coupon payment accounting, amortization of issuance costs, and balance sheet presentation per GAAP/IFRS.

Foreign key linking to security.instrument. Business justification: Debt issuances by the bank ARE securities that must be registered in the instrument master. Funding desk operations, investor relations, prospectus management, regulatory capital reporting (own credit

Foreign key linking to reference.instrument_classification. Business justification: Debt issuances require instrument classification for regulatory capital treatment. Link enables NSFR ASF factor, risk weighting, Tier 2 eligibility, and regulatory reporting (e.g., FFIEC 031).

Foreign key linking to reference.instrument_identifier. Business justification: Debt issuances identified by ISIN/CUSIP for security master data. Link enables pricing validation, maturity tracking, regulatory reporting (e.g., FINRA TRACE), and secondary market monitoring.
Name of the source system where the debt issuance was originally recorded (e.g., Murex, Calypso, Bloomberg AIM). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.
Internal business unit or line of business responsible for managing this debt issuance. Typically Treasury or Corporate Finance.
First date on which the issuer may exercise the call option to redeem the debt instrument early. Applicable only when callable_flag is true.
Price at which the issuer may redeem the debt instrument if the call option is exercised, expressed as a percentage of par value. May include call premium.
Indicates whether the issuer has the right to redeem the debt instrument before maturity. True if call option exists; false otherwise.
Annual interest rate paid on the debt instrument expressed as a decimal percentage. For floating rate instruments, represents the current rate or initial rate at issuance.
Classification of the interest payment structure. Fixed rate remains constant; floating rate resets periodically based on reference rate; zero coupon pays no periodic interest.
Timestamp when this debt issuance record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
Credit rating assigned to the debt instrument by the rating agency. Reflects the agencys assessment of credit risk and default probability.
Name of the credit rating agency that assigned the rating to this debt issuance (e.g., Moodys, S&P, Fitch). Multiple agencies may rate the same instrument.
Indicates whether the debt issuance qualifies as a green bond with proceeds dedicated to environmentally beneficial projects. True if certified green bond; false otherwise.
Date on which the debt instrument was issued and funds were received by the bank. Settlement date for the issuance transaction.

Current lifecycle status of the debt issuance from planning through maturity or early termination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned|priced|issued|outstanding|matured|called|defaulted — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Price at which the debt instrument was issued, expressed as a percentage of par value. Values below 100 indicate discount; above 100 indicate premium.
Timestamp when this debt issuance record was last updated. Tracks the most recent change to any attribute for audit and reconciliation purposes.
Classification of the debt issuance for LCR calculation purposes. Indicates the outflow rate assumption and time bucket for liquidity stress testing.
20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier of the issuing bank entity. Used for regulatory reporting and counterparty identification.
Name of the securities exchange where the debt instrument is listed for trading (e.g., NYSE, LSE, SGX). Null if unlisted or privately placed.
Scheduled date on which the principal amount of the debt instrument becomes due and payable in full.
Original principal amount of the debt issuance in the instruments currency. Face value at issuance before any amortization or repayment.
Classification of the debt issuance for NSFR calculation purposes. Indicates the available stable funding factor based on maturity and counterparty type.
Time period from issuance date to maturity date expressed in standard market convention (e.g., 5Y, 10Y, 30Y). Used for funding maturity profile analysis.
Current principal amount outstanding after accounting for any partial redemptions, amortization, or calls. Used for balance sheet and capital ratio calculations.
URL link to the official prospectus or offering document filed with regulatory authorities. Provides full legal terms and conditions.
First date on which the investor may exercise the put option to require early redemption. Applicable only when puttable_flag is true.
Indicates whether the investor has the right to require early redemption of the debt instrument. True if put option exists; false otherwise.
Date on which the credit rating was assigned or last updated by the rating agency.
Benchmark interest rate index used for floating rate instruments (e.g., SOFR, LIBOR, EURIBOR). Applicable only when coupon_type is floating.
Classification of the debt instrument for Basel III regulatory capital purposes. Determines whether it qualifies as Tier 1, Tier 2, or does not count toward capital ratios.
Credit spread over the reference rate for floating rate instruments, expressed in basis points. Represents the banks credit premium above the risk-free rate.
Comma-separated list of all underwriting syndicate members participating in the debt issuance. Includes co-managers and selling group members.
Name of the lead investment bank or financial institution that underwrote and placed the debt issuance. Primary syndicate member.
Description of how the funds raised from the debt issuance will be used by the bank (e.g., general corporate purposes, refinancing, capital expenditure, green projects).
Unique identifier for the FTP allocation record. Primary key for the FTP allocation transaction.

Foreign key linking to account.certificate_of_deposit. Business justification: FTP methodology allocates funding costs/credits to all interest-bearing deposit products. CDs have distinct tenor/rate profiles requiring separate FTP treatment for profitability measurement and NIM a

Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: FTP allocations applied to accounts in specific currencies for P&L attribution. Link enables multi-currency NIM reporting, FX-adjusted profitability analysis, and currency-specific funding cost alloca

Foreign key linking to account.custodial_account. Business justification: Custodial accounts hold cash balances subject to FTP allocation for profitability measurement. Treasury operations allocate funding costs to custodial cash positions for fiduciary relationship pricing
Reference to the account (loan, deposit, or investment) to which this FTP allocation applies. Links to the specific account receiving the FTP charge or credit.

Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: FTP allocations post to GL accounts for P&L attribution and NIM reporting. Monthly FTP journal entries require proper GL account mapping for financial statement preparation and management reporting.
Reference to the original FTP allocation ID if this record is a reversal or adjustment. Null for original allocations.

Foreign key linking to reference.product_type. Business justification: FTP allocations applied by product type for P&L attribution. Link enables product hierarchy rollup, profitability reporting by product family, and NIM contribution analysis.
Identifier for the FTP curve used to derive the FTP rate. Links to the specific yield curve version applied for this calculation date and currency.
The high-level account type classification indicating whether this is a loan (asset), deposit (liability), or investment account.
The number of days in the accrual period for which the FTP allocation is calculated. Used in conjunction with day_count_convention.
The ALCO reporting category or classification for this FTP allocation. Used for Asset-Liability Management (ALM) and ALCO reporting purposes.
The current status of the FTP allocation record in its lifecycle. Indicates whether the allocation is draft, confirmed, posted to the general ledger, reversed, or adjusted.
Indicates whether this allocation represents an FTP charge (cost to the business line) or an FTP credit (benefit to the business line).
The underlying benchmark rate (e.g., Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR), London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR)) used as the basis for the FTP curve. Expressed as a decimal.
The business line or line of business code to which this FTP allocation is attributed. Used for profitability analysis and Net Interest Margin (NIM) decomposition.
reference: Chart of Accounts and Cost Center Structure

description: The business date on which the FTP allocation was calculated. Represents the effective date for the FTP charge or credit.
The methodology used to calculate the FTP allocation. Options include matched maturity, pool-based, hybrid, or single rate approaches.
Free-text comments or notes related to this FTP allocation. Used for manual adjustments, exceptions, or additional context.
The cost center code responsible for this account and its FTP allocation. Enables Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC) calculation at the cost center level.
The timestamp when this FTP allocation record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.
The credit risk adjustment component in basis points included in the FTP rate. Reflects the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) or credit risk premium.
The customer segment classification for the account holder. Used for segment-level profitability and FTP analysis.
The day count convention used to calculate the FTP amount for the period. Determines how interest accrual days are counted.
reference: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Standards

description: The economic capital allocated to this account balance. Used for Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC) calculation and capital planning.
The calculated FTP charge or credit amount in the account currency. Computed as notional_balance × ftp_rate × day_count_fraction.
The FTP rate applied to the notional balance, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0325 for 3.25%). Derived from the FTP curve for the appropriate tenor and currency.
The liquidity premium component in basis points included in the FTP rate. Reflects the cost or benefit of liquidity for the tenor and product type.
The timestamp when this FTP allocation record was last modified. Audit trail field for change tracking and compliance.
The contribution of this FTP allocation to the overall Net Interest Margin (NIM) for the business line or product. Calculated as FTP amount adjusted for actual interest income or expense.
The principal or notional balance amount of the account on which the FTP rate is applied. Represents the base amount for FTP calculation.
The date on which the FTP allocation was posted to the general ledger. May differ from calculation_date due to accounting period close timing.

The regulatory treatment classification for the account balance. Determines how the position is treated under Basel III, Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB), and other regulatory frameworks.
reference: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Standards

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this FTP allocation record is a reversal of a previous allocation. True if this is a reversal entry, False otherwise.
The risk weight percentage applied to this account balance for Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) calculation. Used in RAROC and capital allocation analysis.
Identifier of the source system that originated this FTP allocation record (e.g., Treasury Management System, Core Banking System). Enables data lineage tracking.
The spread in basis points added to or subtracted from the benchmark rate to arrive at the FTP rate. Represents liquidity premium, credit risk adjustment, or other factors.

The maturity tenor bucket used to determine the FTP rate from the FTP curve. Represents the expected duration or repricing period of the account balance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overnight|1M|3M|6M|1Y|2Y|3Y|5Y|7Y|10Y|15Y|20Y|30Y — 13 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Unique identifier for the FTP rate record.

Foreign key linking to reference.rate_benchmark. Business justification: FTP rates built on benchmark rates (SOFR, SONIA, etc.) for curve construction. Link enables daily rate fixing, benchmark transition management, and spread calculation over risk-free rate.

Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: FTP rates constructed by currency for multi-currency balance sheet. Link enables currency-specific curve construction, FX-adjusted NIM allocation, and cross-currency funding cost comparison.

Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: FTP rates applied to GL account balances for profitability analysis and NIM calculation. FTP allocation process uses GL account balances as basis for transfer pricing charges/credits.
Identifier of the user or system process that created this FTP rate record.

Foreign key linking to reference.product_type. Business justification: FTP rates vary by product type (deposits, loans, mortgages) for NIM allocation. Link enables product-specific FTP curves, profitability analysis by product, and RAROC calculation.
Reference to the FTP rate that supersedes this rate; null if this is the current active rate.
Identifier of the user who approved this FTP rate for activation.
Reference to the FTP curve from which this rate is derived.
Date on which the ALCO formally approved this FTP rate for use.
Reference number or identifier of the ALCO meeting or decision that approved this rate.
Timestamp when this FTP rate was formally approved for use.
Indicates whether this FTP rate applies to asset products (loans, investments) or liability products (deposits, borrowings).
Numeric value of the base rate component expressed in basis points (BPS) or percentage.
Additional basis point adjustment for market basis risk, cross-currency basis, or other technical adjustments.
Timestamp when the FTP rate was calculated or derived from market data and spread components.
Free-text field for additional notes, assumptions, or business context related to this FTP rate.
Fully loaded FTP rate in basis points, representing the sum of base rate and all spread components.
General ledger cost center code for FTP charge or credit allocation.
Timestamp when this FTP rate record was first created in the system.
Credit risk adjustment component in basis points, capturing expected credit loss or risk premium.
Classification of the FTP curve component: base rate (market benchmark), liquidity spread (bank-specific liquidity premium), credit spread (credit risk adjustment), or composite (fully loaded rate).
Date from which this FTP rate becomes effective and applicable to transactions.
Date on which this FTP rate ceases to be effective; null for open-ended rates.
Timestamp when this FTP rate record was last updated or modified.
Business line or segment to which this FTP rate is assigned (e.g., retail banking, commercial banking, wealth management).
Liquidity spread component in basis points, reflecting the bank-specific cost of funding or liquidity premium.
FTP calculation methodology applied: matched-maturity (specific tenor matching), pooled (average cost/yield), or hybrid (combination approach).
Indicates whether this FTP rate is used for NIM decomposition and profitability analysis.
Adjustment in basis points for embedded optionality (e.g., prepayment risk, early withdrawal penalties).

Earliest date on which the issuer can exercise the call option to redeem the debt instrument. Null if not callable.

Flag indicating whether this address is used to determine the party's tax domicile for FATCA (Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act) and CRS (Common Reporting Standard) reporting. True if tax domicile, False otherwise. Applicable for physical address contact types.
reference: FATCA (Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act), CRS (Common Reporting Standard)

description: Business context in which this contact detail or address is used: correspondence (general communication), service (account servicing), billing (invoices and statements), legal (regulatory notices), kyc (identity verification), or emergency (urgent contact).
Date when the contact detail or address was last verified. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: KYC (Know Your Customer) / CDD (Customer Due Diligence) Standards

description: Method used to verify the contact detail or address: document (utility bill, bank statement), third_party (credit bureau, data vendor), customer_declaration, site_visit, or electronic (email link, SMS OTP).
reference: AML (Anti-Money Laundering) / KYC (Know Your Customer) Guidelines

description: Unique identifier for the party contact record. Primary key for the party_contact data product.

business_glossary_term: Contact Type Code List Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.code_list. Business justification: Contact management - contact types (Mobile, Email, Landline, Fax) must be standardized for omnichannel communication, regulatory notifications, and contact preference management.

Foreign key linking to reference.country. Business justification: Contact validation - phone country codes and address validation require validated country reference for contact center routing, regulatory notifications, and international dialing rules.
Reference to the party (customer, counterparty, or entity) to whom this contact information belongs. Links to the party master data product.
Geographic area code or regional prefix for phone numbers. Applicable to phone contact types only.
The number of times an email sent to this contact has bounced (failed delivery). Used to identify invalid or inactive email addresses. Applicable to email contact types only.
Numeric ranking indicating the party's preference order for this contact method. Lower numbers indicate higher preference (1 = most preferred). Used for omnichannel communication routing.
reference: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) Contact Preference Standards

description: The intended purpose or use case for this contact information. Personal for personal communications, business for business-related communications, emergency for urgent notifications, billing for payment-related communications, correspondence for general account communications.
reference: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) Contact Classification Standards

description: Current operational status of the contact information. Active indicates the contact is valid and in use. Inactive indicates the contact is no longer in use. Bounced indicates email delivery failures. Invalid indicates the contact failed validation. Suspended indicates temporary restriction.
reference: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) Contact Management Standards

description: The actual contact information value (phone number, email address, or digital identifier). Format varies by contact type. Classified as restricted PII (Personally Identifiable Information) for phone and email.
reference: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 4, CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act)

description: The date and time when this contact record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Immutable audit field.

Boolean flag indicating whether the party has requested not to be contacted via phone for marketing or solicitation purposes. True if do-not-call is active, False otherwise. Required for TCPA compliance.
reference: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), National Do Not Call Registry

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the party has requested not to be contacted via email for marketing purposes. True if do-not-email is active, False otherwise. Required for CAN-SPAM compliance.
reference: CAN-SPAM Act, GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 21

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the party has requested not to receive physical mail for marketing purposes. True if do-not-mail is active, False otherwise.
reference: DMA (Direct Marketing Association) Guidelines, GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 21

description: The date from which this contact information is valid and active. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Supports temporal tracking of contact information changes.

The date until which this contact information is valid. Null indicates the contact is currently active with no planned end date. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Supports temporal tracking of contact information changes.
Internal phone extension number for work or business phone contacts. Applicable to work phone contact types only.
Boolean flag indicating whether this is the primary or preferred contact method for the party. True if primary, False otherwise.
reference: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) Contact Preference Standards

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the contact information has been verified through a validation process (e.g., email verification link, SMS OTP). True if verified, False otherwise.
reference: KYC (Know Your Customer) Verification Standards, AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Compliance

description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code indicating the preferred language for communications via this contact method (e.g., en for English, es for Spanish, fr for French).
The date of the most recent email bounce. Null if no bounces have occurred. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Applicable to email contact types only.
The date when this contact method was last used to communicate with the party. Null if never contacted. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) Activity Tracking Standards

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the party has consented to receive account statements and regulatory notifications electronically via this contact method. True if opted in, False otherwise.
reference: E-SIGN Act (Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act), UETA (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act)

description: The date when the party provided consent for electronic statements. Null if not opted in. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: E-SIGN Act, UETA (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act)

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the party has consented to receive marketing communications via this contact method. True if opted in, False otherwise. Required for GDPR and CAN-SPAM compliance.
reference: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 6, CAN-SPAM Act, TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act)

description: The date when the party provided consent for marketing communications. Null if not opted in. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) Article 7, CAN-SPAM Act

description: The operational system or channel from which this contact information was originally captured (e.g., Core Banking System, CRM, Mobile App, Branch, Call Center, Online Banking).

The time zone associated with this contact information, using IANA time zone database format (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London). Used to schedule communications at appropriate local times and comply with TCPA calling hour restrictions.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database, TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act)

description: The date and time when this contact record was last modified. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Updated on every change to support change data capture and audit trails.
The date when the contact information was last verified. Null if never verified. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

The method used to verify the contact information. Options include email verification link, SMS one-time password, voice call verification, manual verification by staff, or third-party verification service.
Unique identifier for the party document record. Primary key.

business_glossary_term: Document Type Code List Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.code_list. Business justification: Document type validation - KYC document types (Passport, Driver's License, Utility Bill, Bank Statement) must be standardized for regulatory reporting consistency and document verification workflows.

Foreign key linking to reference.country. Business justification: KYC/AML compliance - passport/ID issuing country must be validated for document verification, sanctions screening, and regulatory reporting. Core identity verification process.
Reference to the party (customer, counterparty, or entity) to whom this document belongs. Links to the party master record.
Identifier of the employee or compliance officer who performed or approved the document verification. Links to the employee master record for audit trail purposes.
Channel or method through which the document was collected from the party. Examples include branch submission, online portal upload, mobile app, email attachment, postal mail, or third-party agent.
Date on which the document was collected or received from the party during the KYC onboarding or periodic review process. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Data classification level indicating the sensitivity and access restrictions for the document. Aligns with the bank's data classification policy.
Timestamp when this party document record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Date on which the document becomes eligible for secure destruction or deletion based on retention policy and regulatory requirements. Nullable if document must be retained indefinitely. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: Data Retention Policy, GDPR Article 5, BSA

description: File format or MIME type of the stored document (e.g., PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, DOCX, XML). Indicates the digital format in which the document is archived.
ISO 639-2 three-letter language code indicating the primary language in which the document is written (e.g., ENG for English, SPA for Spanish, FRA for French, DEU for German, CHI for Chinese).
The unique identification number or reference code printed on the document (e.g., passport number, national ID number, driver's license number, corporate registration number).
Size of the stored document file in kilobytes. Used for storage management and audit purposes.

Secure storage location reference (URI, file path, or vault key) pointing to the digitized copy of the document in the bank's document management system or secure vault. Used to retrieve the document image or PDF for audit and review.
reference: Data Security Standards, SOX, GDPR Article 32

description: Date on which the document expires and is no longer valid for identification or verification purposes. Nullable for documents without expiration (e.g., some corporate certificates). Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Boolean flag indicating whether this document is the primary identity document used for KYC verification (e.g., the main passport or national ID). True if primary, False otherwise.
Date on which the document was originally issued by the authority. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
Name of the government agency, regulatory body, or institution that issued the document (e.g., U.S. Department of State, UK Home Office, Companies House, Ministry of Finance).
Date on which the document was last reviewed or re-verified by compliance or operations. Used to track periodic KYC refresh cycles. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or observations related to the document collection, verification, or review process. Used by compliance officers and relationship managers for context and audit trail.
Boolean flag indicating whether this document is required for regulatory reporting purposes (e.g., FATCA, CRS, SAR filing). True if required for reporting, False otherwise.

Free-text explanation or code describing why the document was rejected during verification (e.g., expired, illegible, fraudulent, does not match party details, insufficient information). Nullable if document is not rejected.

Number of years the document must be retained in the bank's records to comply with regulatory requirements (e.g., 5 years for AML, 7 years for tax records). Drives document lifecycle and archival policies.
reference: BSA, AML Regulations, SOX, GDPR Article 5

description: Date by which the document must be reviewed or re-verified as part of periodic KYC refresh or regulatory compliance requirements. Nullable if no periodic review is required. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: KYC Standards, AML Regulations, CDD Requirements

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the document requires translation into the bank's primary operating language for compliance or operational purposes. True if translation is required, False otherwise.
Status of the document translation process. Indicates whether translation is not required, pending, completed, or certified by a professional translator.
Timestamp when this party document record was last updated or modified. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Date on which the document verification was completed and the verification status was last updated. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

Method or channel used to verify the authenticity of the document. Examples include manual review by compliance officer, biometric matching, third-party verification bureau (e.g., Experian, LexisNexis), automated OCR and data extraction, video KYC, or in-person verification.
Current verification status of the document in the KYC (Know Your Customer) and CDD (Customer Due Diligence) process. Indicates whether the document has been authenticated and accepted.
Unique identifier for the party identifier record. Primary key for this entity.

business_glossary_term: Identifier Type Code List Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.code_list. Business justification: Identifier type standardization - identifier types (CIF, Account Number, Tax ID, SSN, Passport) must be consistent across systems for deduplication, regulatory reporting, and customer matching.
Reference to the party (customer, counterparty, or entity) to whom this identifier belongs. Links to the party master record.
Data classification level indicating the sensitivity and access restrictions for this identifier. Aligns with enterprise data classification policy and determines who can view or use the identifier.
reference: Internal Data Classification Policy, GDPR Article 32, GLBA Safeguards Rule

description: The date and time when this identifier record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Normalized or hashed representation of the identifier value used for deduplication and matching across systems. Supports golden record management and cross-system reconciliation by providing a standardized matching key that accounts for formatting variations.

The date from which the identifier becomes valid and can be used for business operations, regulatory reporting, and cross-system reconciliation. Supports temporal validity tracking for audit and compliance purposes.

The date on which the identifier ceases to be valid. Nullable for identifiers that do not have a predetermined expiration (e.g., permanent tax IDs). Critical for Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance to ensure identifiers are current.
reference: Internal Data Governance Policy, KYC/AML Compliance Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the identifier. Indicates whether the identifier is currently valid and usable for business operations, regulatory reporting, and cross-system reconciliation.

The actual identifier value or number assigned to the party. This is the unique alphanumeric string that represents the party in the external or internal system (e.g., the 20-character LEI code, the 8 or 11-character SWIFT BIC, the 9-digit DUNS number, the CIF account number, the tax identification number, passport number, or national ID number).
reference: ISO 17442 (LEI), ISO 9362 (BIC), DUNS Number Standard, IRS Publication 1179 (TIN), ICAO 9303 (Passport)

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this identifier is the primary or preferred identifier of its type for the party. Used in golden record management and master data management (MDM) processes to determine the authoritative identifier for cross-domain foreign key resolution.
Boolean flag indicating whether the identifier has been verified against the issuing authority or an authoritative source. Critical for KYC/AML compliance and data quality assurance.
reference: KYC/AML Compliance Standards, Internal Data Quality Policy

description: The organization, government agency, or regulatory body that issued or assigned the identifier. Examples include Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) for LEI, SWIFT for BIC, Dun & Bradstreet for DUNS, Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for Tax ID, passport issuing country government, or internal bank system name for legacy identifiers.
reference: ISO 17442 (LEI), ISO 9362 (BIC), DUNS Number Standard, IRS Publication 1179

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country or jurisdiction where the identifier was issued. Used for regulatory reporting and jurisdiction-based risk assessment.
The date and time when this identifier record was last updated or modified. Supports audit trail requirements, change tracking, and data quality monitoring. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
The user ID, employee ID, or system process name that last modified this identifier record. Supports audit trail requirements and accountability for data changes.

Free-text field for additional comments, context, or special instructions related to the identifier. May include information about data quality issues, verification challenges, or special handling requirements.

Numeric ranking indicating the priority or preference order of this identifier among multiple identifiers of the same type for the party. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used in golden record management and cross-system reconciliation when multiple identifiers of the same type exist.

Boolean flag indicating whether this identifier is required for regulatory reporting purposes. Examples include LEI for derivatives reporting under Dodd-Frank Act and European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR), Tax ID for FATCA/CRS reporting, or SWIFT BIC for cross-border payment reporting.
reference: Dodd-Frank Act, EMIR, FATCA, CRS, Basel III Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements

description: The name or code of the operational system from which this identifier record originated. Examples include Core Banking System (e.g., Temenos T24, FIS Profile), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, Loan Origination System (LOS), Trading System (e.g., Murex, Calypso), or external data provider. Supports data lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation.
The unique identifier or primary key of this record in the source operational system. Used for traceability, reconciliation, and troubleshooting data quality issues back to the originating system.

Description of the business context or purpose for which this identifier is used. Examples include regulatory reporting (e.g., Common Reporting Standard (CRS), Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA)), cross-border payments (SWIFT messaging), credit reporting (DUNS), internal customer relationship management (CRM) system integration, or trade finance documentation.
The date on which the identifier was last verified against the issuing authority or authoritative source. Used to track the recency of verification for KYC/AML compliance and data quality monitoring.
reference: KYC/AML Compliance Standards, Internal Data Quality Policy

description: The method or process used to verify the identifier. Examples include manual review by operations staff, automated validation via application programming interface (API) lookup against issuing authority database, third-party verification service, self-attestation by customer, or document review (e.g., scanning passport or tax document).
reference: Internal Data Quality Policy, KYC/AML Compliance Standards

description: The name of the system, service, or authority used to verify the identifier. Examples include GLEIF API for LEI verification, SWIFT directory for BIC verification, Dun & Bradstreet API for DUNS verification, government registry for national ID or passport verification, or internal compliance system name.
Unique identifier for the party-to-party relationship record. Primary key for the relationship hierarchy entity.
Identifier of the employee or relationship manager responsible for managing this party-to-party relationship. Used for accountability, CRM workflows, and performance tracking.
Identifier of the user or system process that last modified this relationship record. Used for audit trails, accountability, and compliance with SOX and data governance requirements.

Identifier of the first party in the relationship. For hierarchical relationships, this is typically the parent, controlling entity, or primary party. For bilateral relationships, this is one side of the association.

business_glossary_term: Relationship Type Code List Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.code_list. Business justification: Relationship management - relationship types (Parent-Subsidiary, Guarantor-Borrower, Ultimate Parent, Affiliate) must be standardized for credit risk aggregation, related-party reporting, and exposure

Indicates whether this relationship should be included in consolidated exposure calculations for regulatory capital and large exposure reporting (Basel III). True for relationships that create economic dependency or control (e.g., parent-subsidiary, guarantor-borrower).
reference: Basel III Large Exposure Framework, CRR Article 4

description: Indicates whether Party A exercises control over Party B, as defined by accounting standards (IFRS 10) or regulatory frameworks (Basel III). Control may exist even without majority ownership (e.g., through voting rights, board representation, or contractual arrangements). Used for consolidated financial reporting and group-level risk aggregation.
reference: IFRS 10, Basel III Large Exposure Framework

description: The date and time when this relationship record was first created in the system. Used for audit trails, data lineage, and regulatory compliance.

Indicates whether this relationship enables cross-sell opportunities (e.g., household members, corporate group entities). Used for CRM analytics, marketing campaigns, and customer lifetime value (CLTV) scoring.

The date on which this relationship became active or legally binding. Used for temporal analysis, historical relationship tracking, and regulatory reporting (e.g., KYC refresh, group structure changes).

The date on which this relationship ends or is scheduled to terminate. Null for open-ended or ongoing relationships. Used for relationship lifecycle management and automated alerts for relationship renewals or reviews.

The depth or tier of this relationship within a hierarchical tree structure. Level 1 represents the top-most parent or ultimate controlling entity. Used for corporate group structure traversal and consolidated exposure calculation. Null for non-hierarchical (bilateral or reciprocal) relationships.
reference: Basel III Large Exposure Framework, IFRS 10

description: Indicates whether this relationship is currently active and in effect. False indicates the relationship has been terminated, suspended, or superseded. Used for filtering current relationships in exposure calculations, CRM views, and regulatory reporting.

business_glossary_term: Know Your Customer (KYC) Last Review Date
description: The date on which this relationship was last reviewed or refreshed as part of KYC/CDD procedures. Used for tracking KYC refresh cycles and ensuring compliance with periodic review requirements.

business_glossary_term: Know Your Customer (KYC) Next Review Date
description: The scheduled date for the next KYC/CDD review or refresh of this relationship. Used for proactive compliance management and automated workflow triggers.

Indicates the KYC verification status of this relationship. Verified indicates the relationship has been validated through KYC/CDD procedures. Pending indicates verification is in progress. Expired indicates the relationship requires re-verification. Used for AML compliance and regulatory reporting.
reference: FATF Recommendations, KYC/CDD Standards, Bank Secrecy Act (BSA)

description: The date and time when this relationship record was last updated or modified. Used for audit trails, change tracking, and data quality monitoring.

Free-text field for additional context, comments, or special instructions related to this relationship. Used for capturing qualitative information that does not fit structured fields (e.g., special approval conditions, relationship history).

The percentage of ownership, control, or beneficial interest that Party A holds in Party B. Applicable for ownership, parent-subsidiary, and beneficial ownership relationships. Used for consolidated exposure calculations and regulatory reporting (e.g., Basel III, IFRS 10). Null for non-ownership relationships.
reference: Basel III Large Exposure Framework, IFRS 10, FATF Beneficial Ownership

description: Indicates whether either party in this relationship is classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or is associated with a PEP. Used for enhanced due diligence requirements and AML compliance.

Indicates whether transactions between these parties are classified as related party transactions under accounting standards (IAS 24) or regulatory frameworks. Used for disclosure requirements, conflict of interest management, and regulatory reporting.
reference: IAS 24, SOX Section 402, Federal Reserve Regulation O

description: Indicates whether the relationship is directional (hierarchical, with a clear parent-child or controlling-controlled structure), bilateral (symmetric association where both parties have equal standing), or reciprocal (mutual obligations or roles).
The unique identifier of this relationship in the source system. Used for traceability, reconciliation, and bi-directional synchronization with operational systems.
The operational system of record from which this relationship was sourced (e.g., Core Banking System, CRM, Loan Origination System). Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and troubleshooting.

Current lifecycle status of the relationship. Active indicates the relationship is in effect. Pending indicates the relationship is awaiting approval or documentation. Under review indicates the relationship is being validated or updated (e.g., during KYC refresh). Terminated indicates the relationship has ended.

The risk classification assigned to this relationship based on AML, credit, or operational risk assessment. Used for risk-based KYC/CDD procedures, enhanced due diligence triggers, and regulatory reporting (e.g., SAR filing thresholds).
reference: FATF Recommendations, Basel III, AML/CFT Standards

description: The role or function that Party A plays in this relationship (e.g., parent, guarantor, account holder, introducer, controlling shareholder, trustee). Provides semantic context for Party A's position.

The role or function that Party B plays in this relationship (e.g., subsidiary, borrower, co-applicant, authorized signatory, beneficial owner, beneficiary). Provides semantic context for Party B's position.

The date on which this relationship was last screened against sanctions lists (e.g., OFAC, UN, EU). Used for tracking screening frequency and ensuring compliance with continuous monitoring requirements.

Indicates the result of sanctions screening for this relationship. Clear indicates no sanctions matches. Match indicates a potential or confirmed sanctions hit. Pending indicates screening is in progress. Used for AML compliance and regulatory reporting.
reference: OFAC, FATF Recommendations, Bank Secrecy Act (BSA)

description: Reference identifier or URI to the legal or supporting documentation that evidences this relationship (e.g., shareholder agreement, power of attorney document, joint account application, beneficial ownership declaration). Used for audit trails and regulatory compliance (KYC/AML).
reference: FATF Recommendations, KYC/CDD Standards, Bank Secrecy Act (BSA)

description: Primary key for marketing_campaign
Reference to a parent or umbrella campaign if this is a sub-campaign or variant. Nullable for standalone campaigns.
Self-referencing FK on marketing_campaign (parent_marketing_campaign_id)
Number of unique customers or prospects actually reached by the campaign.
Total amount actually spent on the campaign to date in the base currency.
Timestamp when the campaign was approved for execution. Nullable if not yet approved.
Total allocated budget for the campaign in the base currency.
Banking business unit or division sponsoring the campaign.
Externally-known unique business identifier for the campaign, used in tracking URLs, promotional materials, and cross-system references.
Human-readable name of the marketing campaign for internal reference and reporting.
Primary business goal the campaign is designed to achieve.
Name or identifier of the marketing manager or team responsible for the campaign.
Current lifecycle status of the marketing campaign.
Classification of the campaign by primary marketing channel or method used.
Primary communication channel used to deliver the campaign.
Secondary or supporting communication channel used in the campaign. Nullable if single-channel.
Timestamp when the campaign was marked as completed. Nullable for ongoing or cancelled campaigns.
Number of customers who completed the desired action (e.g., opened account, applied for product).
Timestamp when the campaign record was first created in the system.
Version identifier for the creative assets (copy, images, design) used in the campaign.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for budget and spend amounts.
Date when the campaign is scheduled to conclude. Nullable for ongoing campaigns.
Geographic market or region targeted by the campaign (e.g., national, regional, branch-specific).
URL of the dedicated landing page for the campaign.
Timestamp when the campaign was actually launched and became active. Nullable if not yet launched.
Timestamp when the campaign record was last updated.
Free-text notes or comments about the campaign for internal reference.
Unique promotional code customers can use to redeem the campaign offer.
Detailed description of the promotional offer or value proposition presented in the campaign.
Indicates whether customer opt-in consent is required for this campaign per privacy regulations.
Banking product category being promoted (e.g., credit cards, mortgages, investment products, business loans).
Date when regulatory or compliance approval was granted. Nullable if not required.
Indicates whether the campaign required regulatory or compliance review before launch.
Number of customers who responded to the campaign (clicked, replied, or engaged).
Date when the campaign becomes active and begins execution.
Number of customers or prospects targeted by this campaign.
Description of the customer segment or persona this campaign is targeting (e.g., high-net-worth individuals, small business owners, millennials).
Indicates whether this campaign includes a test/control group for A/B testing or effectiveness measurement.
URL with tracking parameters used to measure campaign click-through and conversions.
Unique identifier for each party segment assignment record. Primary key for the party segment assignment entity.

Foreign key linking to ledger.profit_center. Business justification: Customer segments are mapped to profit centers for revenue attribution, segment P&L reporting, RAROC calculation, and management reporting. Essential for line-of-business profitability analysis and st
Reference to the branch or service center associated with this segment assignment, supporting geographic and organizational segmentation.
Reference to the relationship manager or account officer assigned to parties in this segment, supporting personalized service delivery.

business_glossary_term: Line Of Business Code List Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.code_list. Business justification: LOB standardization for segment assignment - line of business codes must be consistent for segment performance reporting, cross-LOB analytics, and customer profitability analysis.
Reference to the party (customer, counterparty, or entity) being assigned to a segment. Links to the party master entity.
Reference to the employee who created or approved the segment assignment, supporting accountability and audit trail requirements.
Reference to the customer segment classification being assigned. Links to the customer segment reference entity.
Date when the segment assignment was formally approved, supporting audit trail and governance requirements.
Date when the segment assignment was created or recorded in the system, distinct from the effective date.
Methodology used to assign the party to the segment, indicating whether it was automated through business rules, manually overridden by staff, or driven by analytical models.
Business justification or rationale for the segment assignment, capturing why the party was placed in this particular segment.
Current lifecycle status of the segment assignment indicating whether it is currently in effect, pending approval, or has been terminated.
Precise date and time when the segment assignment was created or recorded, supporting detailed audit trail and sequencing requirements.
Assets Under Management band or range associated with the segment assignment, particularly relevant for wealth management and private banking segments.
Boolean flag indicating whether parties in this segment assignment are eligible for targeted marketing campaigns and promotional activities.
Customer Lifetime Value cohort classification associated with this segment assignment, enabling CLTV-based analysis and targeted strategies.
Free-text comments or notes providing additional context, justification, or special considerations related to the segment assignment.
Statistical confidence level (expressed as percentage) associated with the segment assignment, indicating the reliability of the classification.
Date when the segment assignment becomes active and valid for business operations, reporting, and analytics.
Date when the segment assignment ceases to be valid. Null indicates an open-ended assignment with no predetermined end date.
Geographic region or market associated with the segment assignment, supporting regional segmentation and market analysis.
Boolean flag indicating whether this is the currently active segment assignment for the party. True indicates the current assignment; False indicates a historical or superseded assignment.
Boolean flag indicating whether this is the primary segment assignment when a party may belong to multiple segments simultaneously.
Name of the analytical or segmentation model used to determine the segment assignment (e.g., Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) Model, Risk-Based Segmentation Model).
Reference identifier for the analytical model execution that generated this segment assignment, enabling traceability to specific model runs for audit and validation purposes.
Numerical score produced by the segmentation model indicating the strength or confidence of the segment assignment.
Version identifier of the segmentation model used, supporting model governance and change tracking over time.
Numerical ranking indicating the priority or precedence of this segment assignment when multiple concurrent assignments exist for the same party.
Timestamp when this segment assignment record was first created in the data platform, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.
Timestamp when this segment assignment record was last modified in the data platform, supporting change tracking and audit requirements.
Revenue band or range associated with the segment assignment, supporting revenue-based segmentation strategies.
Date when the segment assignment is scheduled for review or reassessment, supporting periodic validation and refresh cycles.
Frequency in months at which the segment assignment should be reviewed and potentially updated, supporting ongoing segmentation accuracy.
Risk classification associated with the segment assignment, supporting risk-based customer management and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance requirements.
reference: Risk Management Framework, Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations

description: Hierarchical tier classification within the segment, supporting multi-level segmentation strategies (e.g., Tier 1 for highest value customers).
Service level or tier associated with the segment assignment, determining the level of service, support, and benefits provided to the party.
Name or identifier of the source system that originated or provided the segment assignment data, supporting data lineage and reconciliation.
Date when the party transitioned from the previous segment to the current segment, supporting segment migration analysis.
Business reason or trigger for the segment transition, capturing why the party moved from one segment to another.
Unique identifier for the prospect record. Primary key.
Employee identifier of the relationship manager or sales representative assigned to cultivate and convert this prospect.

Foreign key linking to reference.country. Business justification: Lead qualification - prospect country drives regulatory feasibility assessment, sanctions screening, market entry evaluation, and sales territory assignment. Core sales and compliance process.
Identifier of the specific marketing campaign or initiative that generated this prospect lead for attribution and ROI (Return on Investment) tracking.

business_glossary_term: Lead Source Code List Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.code_list. Business justification: Marketing attribution - lead sources (Referral, Campaign, Walk-in, Digital, Partner) must be standardized for marketing ROI analysis, channel effectiveness measurement, and customer acquisition cost t
Party identifier assigned to the prospect upon successful conversion to customer status linking the prospect record to the customer master record.
Party identifier of the existing customer or partner who referred this prospect for relationship attribution and incentive tracking.
Self-referencing FK on prospect (source_prospect_id)
Code of the branch or office location responsible for this prospect relationship.
Date when the prospect was successfully converted to an active customer and onboarding was completed.
Timestamp when the prospect record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether the prospect has provided consent for data collection and processing in accordance with privacy regulations.
Date when the prospect was formally disqualified and removed from active pursuit.

Reference to the parent loan facility for which this amortization schedule was generated. Links each schedule entry to its originating loan contract.
Number of days in the interest accrual period for this installment. Calculated based on the day count convention specified in the loan agreement (e.g., 30/360, Actual/365, Actual/Actual).
End date of the interest accrual period for this installment. Typically the due date of this payment. Used to calculate the number of days for interest accrual.
Start date of the interest accrual period for this installment. Typically the day after the previous payment due date or the loan disbursement date for the first installment.
Actual interest amount applied from the received payment. May differ from scheduled interest due to payment timing, rate changes, or payment allocation rules.
Actual total amount received for this installment. May differ from scheduled amount due to partial payments, prepayments, or payment shortfalls. Null if no payment has been received.

Type of amortization method used for this schedule. Level payment maintains constant total payments; level principal maintains constant principal payments; bullet has principal due at maturity; balloon has a large final payment; custom follows a non-standard pattern.
Outstanding principal balance at the start of this payment period, before the current installment is applied. Represents the loan balance carried forward from the previous period.

Method used to calculate the number of days in the accrual period and the year basis for interest calculations. Standard conventions include 30/360, Actual/365, Actual/360, and Actual/Actual.

Number of days this payment is overdue, calculated as the difference between current date (or actual payment date) and the due date. Zero or null if payment is current or paid on time. Critical metric for delinquency tracking and credit risk assessment.
Scheduled date on which this installment payment is contractually due. Used for payment processing, delinquency tracking, and cash flow forecasting.
Outstanding principal balance remaining after this scheduled payment is applied. Calculated as beginning balance minus scheduled principal amount. Becomes the beginning balance for the next period.
Sequential number of this payment installment within the loan's repayment schedule. Starts at 1 for the first payment and increments for each subsequent scheduled payment.

Annual interest rate in effect for this payment period, expressed as a decimal. May vary across installments for variable-rate loans or after rate resets. Used to calculate the scheduled interest amount.
Indicates whether this is the final scheduled payment for the loan. True for the last installment that brings the ending balance to zero. Used to identify loan maturity and schedule completion.

Indicates whether this installment is part of a restructured payment schedule. True if the loan has been modified after origination due to borrower hardship, forbearance, or other restructuring events. Critical for regulatory reporting and credit risk classification.

Late payment fee assessed for this installment if payment was received after the due date. Calculated according to the loan agreement's late fee provisions. Null if payment was on time or no late fee was assessed.
Frequency at which payments are scheduled for this loan. Determines the interval between installments and affects the amortization calculation.

Method by which the actual payment was received for this installment. Includes ACH (Automated Clearing House), wire transfer, check, cash, card payment, or internal account transfer. Null if payment has not been received.

Current status of this scheduled installment payment. Tracks whether the payment is still scheduled, has been paid in full, partially paid, is overdue, has been waived, or has been deferred to a future date.

Additional principal amount paid beyond the scheduled principal for this installment. Represents voluntary prepayments that reduce the outstanding balance faster than scheduled. Null if no prepayment occurred.
Date on which the loan restructuring became effective, if applicable. Null for non-restructured installments. Used to track troubled debt restructuring (TDR) events and assess credit quality.
Date on which this version of the amortization schedule was generated or regenerated. Updated whenever the schedule is recalculated due to loan modifications or rate changes.

Version number of this amortization schedule. Increments each time the schedule is regenerated due to loan modifications, restructuring, rate resets, or payment plan changes. Version 1 is the original schedule at loan origination.
Any contractually scheduled fees or charges included in this installment, such as servicing fees, insurance premiums, or other recurring charges.
Contractually scheduled interest charge for this payment period. Calculated based on the beginning balance, interest rate, and accrual period. Represents the cost of borrowing for this period.
Contractually scheduled principal reduction amount for this installment. This portion of the payment reduces the outstanding loan balance.
Total amount due for this installment, calculated as the sum of scheduled principal, interest, and fees. This is the amount the borrower is contractually obligated to pay on the due date.
Timestamp when this amortization schedule entry was last modified. Updated whenever payment status changes, actual payment information is recorded, or schedule adjustments are made.

Total amount of scheduled payment that was waived or forgiven for this installment. May include waived principal, interest, or fees due to loan modifications, hardship programs, or settlement agreements.

Initial pricing spread over the reference rate (SOFR, LIBOR, etc.) in basis points at syndication launch. Used to track pricing flex if terms were adjusted during marketing.
